Dissolve triangles into polygons by group

Source: R/tri_dissolve.R
tri_dissolve.Rd

Merge the triangles of a triangle pool into one MULTIPOLYGON per group, along shared triangle edges. With the default group, the triangles of each feature are dissolved back into that feature's polygons.

Usage

tri_dissolve(x, group = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A wkpool_tri.

group

Integer group id per triangle (1-based, NA to leave a triangle out). The default is the triangles' feature, or one group when the pool has no feature.

...

Unused.

Value

A wk::wkb() vector of MULTIPOLYGON, one per group id from 1 to the largest in group, with the pool's crs.

Details

group is one integer per triangle: a dense, 1-based group id, with NA for a triangle that belongs to no group (it is left out, and its edges become boundary). This is the set_id of a labelled mesh, so a mesh labelled by the covering input features (an overlay) dissolves into its pieces with tri_dissolve(x, set_id), while the table from set to features is kept by the caller. Element k of the result is group k; a group id with no triangles gives MULTIPOLYGON EMPTY.

Triangles must be counter-clockwise and form a triangulation (no overlaps), with adjacent triangles sharing vertex ids: run merge_coincident() first on a pool whose triangles do not already share vertices. Triangles are joined only across an edge whose two triangles share both of its vertex ids, so triangles that touch at a vertex or along part of an edge stay separate.

Rings follow the edges of the triangles, so pieces that touch share vertices exactly. Outer rings are counter-clockwise and holes clockwise. A group has one polygon for each edge-connected part, and a boundary that passes through a vertex twice (a hole touching its outer ring, for example) is split there, so every ring is simple and rings meet only at points. Only x and y are used.

Examples

x <- wk::as_wkb(c(
  "POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 1, 0 0), (0.2 0.3, 0.2 0.5, 0.4 0.5, 0.2 0.3))",
  "POLYGON ((1 0, 2 0, 2 1, 1 1, 1 0))"
))
if (requireNamespace("decido", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tri <- merge_coincident(pool_triangulate(establish_topology(x)))
  ## back to the input polygons
  wk::as_wkt(tri_dissolve(tri))
  ## everything as one polygon, with the hole kept
  wk::as_wkt(tri_dissolve(tri, rep(1L, length(tri))))
}
#> <wk_wkt[1]>
#> [1] MULTIPOLYGON (((0 1, 0 0, 1 0, 2 0, 2 1, 1 1...
